en: Therīgāthā 7.3 Sattakanipāta: The Verses of the Elder Nun Upacālā I am no longer subject to birth; My rebirth has been eradicated. Having realized for myself through direct knowledge, I have attained parinibbāna in this very life. I am no longer subject to old age; My rebirth has been eradicated. Having realized for myself through direct knowledge, I have attained parinibbāna in this very life. I am no longer subject to death; My rebirth has been eradicated. Having realized for myself through direct knowledge, I have attained parinibbāna in this very life. I am no longer subject to sorrow; My rebirth has been eradicated. Having realized for myself through direct knowledge, I have attained parinibbāna in this very life. I am no longer subject to lamentation; My rebirth has been eradicated. Having realized for myself through direct knowledge, I have attained parinibbāna in this very life. I am no longer subject to suffering; My rebirth has been eradicated. Having realized for myself through direct knowledge, I have attained parinibbāna in this very life. I am no longer subject to defilement; My rebirth has been eradicated. Having realized for myself through direct knowledge, I have attained parinibbāna in this very life.
“Possessed of mindfulness and possessed of vision,
the bhikkhunī with developed faculties has penetrated the state of peace.”
"Practiced by no base men.
"Why do you not approve of birth?
One who is born enjoys sensual pleasures;"
“Enjoy the delights of sensual pleasure;
do not be one who regrets it later.
“For one who is born, death occurs.”
The cutting off of hands and feet,
the suffering of execution and bondage—
one who is born [into such a state] undergoes misery.
There is one born in the Sakya clan,
the unconquered Sambuddha;
he taught the Dhamma to me.
The transcendence of birth;
suffering, the arising of suffering,
and the transcendence of suffering.
The noble eightfold path that leads to the stilling of suffering;
having heard his words, I—
Dwelling delighted in the Teaching,
I have attained the three knowledges and fulfilled the Buddha’s instruction.
Delight is destroyed everywhere,
the mass of darkness is shattered;
know this thus, O Evil One!
“You are slain, O End-maker!
… [Thus spoke] the Elder Nun Upacālā.
The Seventh Chapter is concluded.
